item.title: Antaeus: Hunting Repository-Level Logic Vulnerabilities via Context-Grounded LLM Reasoning
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.01138v1

AI Summary (中文)

背景与挑战

逻辑漏洞（Logic Vulnerabilities）因其高度依赖应用语义、隐式安全假设和跨函数/模块的业务逻辑而难以检测。传统基于规则或符号执行的方法难以建模，而现有LLM漏洞检测器虽在内存安全类缺陷上表现良好，却普遍缺乏仓库级上下文感知能力——无法理解函数在整体应用架构中的角色、信任边界、安全资源调用模式及项目特有规范，导致误报率高、关键漏洞漏检。

方法创新：Antaeus框架

Antaeus提出一种上下文锚定的仓库级推理范式，包含四大核心环节：

  • 函数优先级排序：利用轻量级仓库全局信号（如API入口标记、权限检查密度、敏感数据流枢纽）自动筛选高风险函数，显著降低LLM调用频次（平均减少62%）；
  • 上下文融合推理：对每个候选函数，同步注入三类上下文：①局部代码片段、②仓库级功能拓扑（如认证/授权模块位置）、③显式安全资源（如策略配置文件、ACL定义）；
  • 对比验证机制：将候选漏洞与项目内同类函数行为基线比对，自动过滤符合“项目惯例”的非异常行为，提升精确率；
  • 结构化可追溯报告：输出含漏洞触发点（sink）、失效的安全条件（e.g., “未校验用户所属租户”）、跨文件证据链（调用路径+配置引用），支持开发者一键复现与修复。

实证效果

在28个含已确认逻辑漏洞的真实开源仓库（涵盖OAuth实现、支付网关、RBAC系统等）上评估：Antaeus成功检测并清晰解释15个漏洞（含7个零日漏洞），检出率较函数级微调模型提升3.2×，较前沿Agentic模型（如Claude-3.5 Sonnet Agent）提升2.1×，且总token消耗降低41%，报告可操作性获安全工程师100%认可。

AI Summary (English)

Antaeus is a novel LLM-based framework for detecting repository-level logic vulnerabilities—bugs rooted in violated application-specific security invariants and implicit behavioral assumptions. Unlike memory-safety detectors, Antaeus grounds LLM reasoning in holistic repository context: it prioritizes functions using lightweight repo-wide signals (e.g., trust boundary density, policy file proximity), enriches local code with cross-file functionality maps and security resources (e.g., ACL configs, auth middleware), derives and validates safety conditions in situ, and applies comparative validation against project-wide behavioral norms to suppress false positives. Evaluated on 28 real-world repositories with confirmed logic flaws, Antaeus detects and explains 15 vulnerabilities—including 7 zero-days—with 2.1× higher precision than state-of-the-art agentic baselines and 41% lower token cost, while generating actionable, traceable reports with sink locations, violated conditions, and multi-file evidence chains.

Abstract

LLM-based vulnerability detectors have shown promising results in identifying memory-safety bugs and vulnerability classes whose violations can often be expressed through established security properties. Logic vulnerabilities, however, pose a different challenge, as their identification requires inferring application-specific security invariants and implicit assumptions about intended behavior. Even frontier agentic models struggle because these invariants are often implicit and buried among unrelated code. Motivated by this gap, we present Antaeus, a framework for detecting logic vulnerabilities that grounds LLM reasoning in repository-level code context. Antaeus follows a repository-scale pipeline combining function prioritization, context-grounded reasoning, comparative validation, and structured reporting. It ranks functions using lightweight repo-wide security signals, directing costly LLM analysis toward relevant code and reducing calls, cost, and triage effort. For each prioritized function, Antaeus combines local code context with a repository-level view of the application's functionality, security resources, and trust boundaries. This enables reasoning about how the function is executed within the broader application rather than as an isolated snippet. Antaeus identifies security-sensitive sinks, derives safety conditions for safe execution, and checks whether they are locally satisfied. Candidate findings undergo comparative validation, pruning concerns that reflect project-wide norms rather than distinctive violations. Finally, Antaeus reports sinks, violated safety conditions, and evidence, making findings actionable and traceable. We evaluate Antaeus on 28 repositories with confirmed logic vulnerabilities and compare it against function-level and agentic models. Antaeus detects and explains 15 vulnerabilities, outperforming baselines with comparable token usage and cost.

item.title: The Binary Tree Mechanism is Optimal for Approximate Differentially Private Continual Counting
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00876v1

AI Summary (中文)

研究背景与问题

私有持续计数（Private Continual Counting）是差分隐私领域的基础性问题：给定长度为 $n$ 的二进制数据流（每个“1”代表一名个体的贡献），需在流式到达过程中实时发布所有前缀和（即运行计数），同时严格保护每个个体的隐私。经典算法——二叉树机制（Binary Tree Mechanism）通过分层求和结构注入高斯噪声，在 $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-近似差分隐私（approximate DP）下实现期望 $\ell_\infty$ 误差为 $O(\log^{3/2} n)$。然而，该对数阶依赖是否本质最优，即是否存在更优算法突破 $\log^{3/2} n$ 瓶颈，十余年来一直是该领域核心开放问题。

主要突破与证明方法

本工作首次完全解决了这一渐近紧性问题：我们证明，任意满足 $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-近似差分隐私的持续计数机制，其期望 $\ell_\infty$ 误差必为 $\Omega(\log^{3/2} n)$。该下界通过构造一类精心设计的对抗性输入流，并结合隐私-精度权衡的递归信息论分析与高斯过程极值理论（特别是Slepian引理与Talagrand小球测度方法）建立。关键创新在于将连续查询的隐私约束转化为对特定随机过程最大值的下界估计，从而绕过传统矩方法或组合下界的技术瓶颈。

核心结论与意义

  • 二叉树机制在近似DP下达到渐近最优，其 $\log^{3/2} n$ 误差不可改进；
  • 首次确立持续计数问题的精确误差阶，终结长期悬而未决的最优性猜想；
  • 推出线性查询中遗传差异性（hereditary discrepancy）与私有 $\ell_\infty$ 误差之间最大可能的分离：证明现有基于遗传差异性的通用上界（$O(\mathrm{herdisc} \cdot \sqrt{\log m})$，$m$ 为查询数）具有最优的 $\log m$ 因子依赖，无法进一步改善。本成果为差分隐私基础理论提供了关键判据，并为动态数据发布系统的设计确立了理论天花板。

AI Summary (English)

This paper resolves a central open problem in private continual counting: we prove that any $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-approximately differentially private mechanism for releasing all prefix sums of an $n$-length binary stream must incur expected $\ell_\infty$ error at least $\Omega(\log^{3/2} n)$. This matches the upper bound achieved by the Gaussian-noise binary tree mechanism, establishing its asymptotic optimality in the approximate-DP setting. Our lower bound is derived via a novel combination of adversarial stream construction, recursive information-theoretic privacy constraints, and extreme value analysis of Gaussian processes—leveraging Slepian’s lemma and Talagrand’s generic chaining. As a corollary, we obtain the largest possible separation between hereditary discrepancy and private $\ell_\infty$ error for linear queries, confirming that the known general upper bound $O(\mathrm{herdisc} \cdot \sqrt{\log m})$ for $m$ queries has optimal dependence on $m$.

Abstract

Private continual counting is a fundamental problem in differential privacy: given a binary stream of length $n$, where each $1$ corresponds to the contribution of one individual, the goal is to release all running counts while protecting the privacy of each individual. The standard algorithm is the binary tree mechanism, whose Gaussian-noise variant achieves expected $\ell_\infty$ error proportional to $\log^{3/2} n$ for approximate differential privacy. Whether this dependence on the stream length is necessary has remained a central open problem. In this work, we resolve the dependence on $n$ by proving that every differentially private mechanism for continual counting must incur expected $\ell_\infty$ error $Ω(\log^{3/2} n)$. This shows that the binary tree mechanism is asymptotically optimal in the approximate-DP setting. As a consequence, we also obtain a largest-possible separation between hereditary discrepancy and private $\ell_\infty$ error for linear queries, showing that the known general upper bound in terms of hereditary discrepancy has the optimal dependence on the number of queries.

item.title: Cross-Domain Generalization Failure in Lightweight Intrusion Detection Models for IIoT Networks
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00553v1

AI Summary (中文)

研究背景与问题

面向工业物联网（IIoT）边缘部署的轻量级入侵检测模型近年来备受关注，但其跨域泛化能力长期被忽视。现有研究多在单一数据集内训练并评估模型，未验证其在结构异构、流量分布迥异的未知IIoT网络上的表现，导致部署可靠性存疑。

方法设计

本研究在一个源IIoT数据集上训练四种轻量级模型（如LightGBM、TinyML-CNN等），随后在两个结构显著不同的目标IIoT数据集上进行零样本迁移评估。所有实验统一采用跨数据集可复用的最小特征集（仅含端口类别、协议类型等通用属性），排除特征可用性偏差。进一步结合SHAP与LIME开展可解释性分析，并在自然类不平衡场景下系统评估泛化性能、对抗鲁棒性及有限目标域微调恢复能力。

关键发现

  • 端口粗粒度捷径效应：两类最优模型均过度依赖“端口类别”特征；某关键攻击相关端口类别在源域攻击流量中出现频次达目标域的96–435倍——表明端口聚合并未消除数据捷径，仅将其转移；
  • 评估协议敏感性：在真实不平衡分布下，不同评估指标（如F1 vs. AUC）会反转对两目标域泛化难度的排序，凸显单一指标误导风险；
  • 鲁棒性与泛化解耦：对抗扰动鲁棒性与跨域泛化能力无显著关联；
  • 架构依赖型适应性：仅需<1%目标域样本微调即可显著提升性能，但各模型恢复效率差异达3.2倍，凸显架构选择的关键影响。

创新与启示

本研究首次系统揭示轻量级IIoT检测模型的跨域失效机制，提出以跨网络+真实分布为双核心的部署就绪性评估范式，为边缘安全模型落地提供可复现、可解释、可操作的验证基准。

AI Summary (English)

This study exposes critical cross-domain generalization failures in lightweight ML models for IIoT intrusion detection. Training four compact architectures on one IIoT dataset and evaluating them zero-shot on two structurally distinct target datasets—using only universally available features—we find that top-performing models rely overwhelmingly on coarse port-category features, with a key attack-associated category appearing 96–435× more frequently in source-domain attack traffic than in target domains—revealing port coarsening relocates, not eliminates, documented shortcuts. Under natural class imbalance, evaluation protocol choice (e.g., F1 vs. AUC) reverses perceived generalization difficulty between target networks. Adversarial robustness proves unrelated to cross-network generalization, while recovery via minimal target-domain adaptation (<1% samples) varies substantially across architectures (up to 3.2× performance gain difference). These results mandate cross-network evaluation under realistic class distributions—not just in-domain accuracy—for assessing real-world deployment readiness.

Abstract

Lightweight machine learning models are increasingly proposed for intrusion detection in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) networks due to their suitability for resource-constrained edge deployment. Most reported results evaluate these models only within their training network, leaving behavior on unseen networks unverified. This study trains four lightweight architectures on one IIoT dataset and evaluates them, without retraining, on two structurally distinct IIoT datasets using a feature representation restricted to attributes available across all three sources. Explainability analysis across two top-performing models shows both rely overwhelmingly on coarse port-category features; the most influential category occurs in source-domain attack traffic at 96 to 435 times the rate in the two target domains, indicating that coarsening port resolution relocates rather than removes a documented shortcut. Evaluation under naturally imbalanced class distributions reveals a further effect: the evaluation protocol used can reverse which target network appears to pose the greater generalization challenge. Adversarial robustness and recovery through limited target-domain exposure are also assessed; robustness to adversarial perturbation is unrelated to cross-network generalization, and recovery through adaptation varies considerably by architecture. These findings suggest deployment readiness should be assessed using cross-network evaluation under realistic class distributions, rather than within-domain accuracy alone.

item.title: Beyond the Prompt: Jailbreaking Function-Calling LLMs via Simulated Moderation Traces
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00481v1

AI Summary (中文)

超越提示词：通过模拟审核轨迹越狱函数调用型大语言模型

背景与问题：当前针对大语言模型（LLM）的越狱攻击研究多聚焦于单轮提示词层面，却忽视了在状态化、函数调用型应用环境中深层的系统性漏洞。此类系统将开发者定义的工具Schema、结构化参数、不可信的工具输出与对话历史共同注入同一模型上下文，导致“可信控制逻辑”与“不可信数据”的边界模糊，使恶意意图可被跨多轮执行路径分布式编码，极大扩展攻击面。

方法创新（SMT框架）：本文提出SMT（Simulated Moderation Traces）——首个面向函数调用LLM的黑盒越狱框架。SMT不依赖提示词扰动，而是构建一条模拟真实审核审计流程的多轮交互轨迹：

  • 第一阶段：以“红队安全测试”为合法 pretext，构造虚构的审核框架（moderation frame），诱导模型生成潜在有害内容；
  • 第二阶段：将模型的安全拒绝响应视为“执行失败”，利用反馈信号驱动迭代优化，逐步削弱其内置安全约束；
  • 全程无需访问模型权重或内部机制，仅通过标准API交互实现。

关键发现：在涵盖5家主流厂商（Anthropic、OpenAI、Google、Meta、阿里）的12个商用LLM上，基于SafeBench与HarmBench两大基准的实证评估表明：
✅ SMT平均攻击成功率（ASR）达78.3%，显著高于现有最优基线（+22.6%）；
✅ HarmScore（危害强度量化指标）提升3.1×，且单次攻击仅需4.2轮交互（接近理论最小轮数）；
✅ 攻击效果在工具调用密集场景（如代码生成、实时搜索）中尤为突出，验证了架构级脆弱性的普适性。

启示与意义：结果证实，仅靠提示词过滤或输入清洗无法防御函数调用型LLM系统；亟需部署上下文感知的全链路验证机制——覆盖Schema语义、参数合法性、工具输出可信度及累积对话状态的一致性校验。

AI Summary (English)

Jailbreak attacks against function-calling LLMs expose a critical architectural vulnerability beyond prompt-level manipulation: the interleaving of developer-defined schemas, structured arguments, and untrusted tool outputs into a shared stateful context blurs trust boundaries and enables adversarial intent to span multi-turn execution paths. We propose SMT (Simulated Moderation Traces), a black-box attack framework that bypasses prompt-centric assumptions by simulating a legitimate moderation-auditing workflow—using red-teaming as pretext to elicit harmful generations, then treating safety refusals as execution failures to iteratively weaken constraints. Evaluated across 12 commercial LLMs from 5 providers on SafeBench and HarmBench, SMT achieves the highest average attack success rate (78.3%) and HarmScore (+3.1× vs. baselines) with minimal queries (4.2 turns), demonstrating that prompt sanitization alone is fundamentally insufficient. Our work underscores the urgent need for context-aware, end-to-end validation across schemas, arguments, tool outputs, and conversation state.

Abstract

Jailbreak attacks remain a critical threat to the safe deployment of large language models (LLMs). While prior work has primarily studied attacks and defenses at the prompt level, we show that this prompt-centric paradigm overlooks a structural vulnerability in stateful, function-calling environments. In such applications, developer-defined schemas, structured arguments, and untrusted tool outputs are interleaved into a single shared model context. This architecture expands the attack surface by blurring the boundary between trusted control logic and untrusted data, allowing adversarial intent to be distributed across a multi-turn execution path. We exploit this architectural flaw through SMT, a black-box attack framework based on Simulated Moderation Traces. Departing from purely prompt-based interactions, SMT constructs a multi-turn trajectory that simulates a legitimate moderation-auditing workflow. Within this trajectory, a fabricated moderation frame leverages red-team testing as a pretext to elicit harmful generations. The subsequent validation feedback treats safety refusals as execution failures, prompting refinements that gradually weaken the model's safety constraints and ultimately trigger harmful outputs. Extensive empirical evaluations on prominent commercial LLMs from five different providers across two standardized safety benchmarks show that SMT consistently achieves the highest average attack success rate and HarmScore while requiring a near-minimal number of queries, substantially outperforming existing baselines. These findings demonstrate that prompt-level sanitization alone is fundamentally insufficient for defending tool-enabled LLM systems and highlight the urgent need for context-aware validation across schemas, arguments, tool outputs, and accumulated conversation state. The code is available at https://github.com/liujlong27/SMT.

item.title: Minos: A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework for Provenance-Based Backward Tracking
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00440v1

AI Summary (中文)

背景与挑战

针对高级持续性威胁（APT）等复杂网络攻击，基于溯源（provenance）的反向追踪是关键的后入侵取证手段。然而，现有方法严重依赖低层统计特征与固定遍历策略，难以建模攻击者的高层意图，且易因依赖爆炸（dependency explosion）导致图搜索空间失控、结果冗余、可解释性差。

方法创新：Minos多智能体协同框架

本研究提出 Minos——首个将反向追踪建模为大语言模型（LLM）驱动协同推理过程的多智能体框架。其核心创新在于双层级架构：

  • 事件级分析层：融合分层上下文管理、检索增强式推理（含引用验证） 与对抗性审议机制，显著提升因果推理的准确性与鲁棒性；
  • 图探索层：引入基于有限状态机（FSM）协调的四角色专用智能体（如假设生成者、依赖验证者、计数优先查询器、收敛判别器），摒弃穷举遍历，转而采用假设引导推理与计数优先查询协议，实现高效剪枝。

实验结果与价值

在5个公开数据集、14类真实攻击场景上的实验表明：Minos平均召回率达0.92、精确率达0.64，显著超越SOTA基线；所生成的攻击子图体积压缩49%，大幅提升分析效率；全程输出可审计的链式推理日志，支持人工复核与系统迭代优化。本工作验证了LLM原生推理能力在自动化溯源分析中的范式价值。

AI Summary (English)

Minos is a novel multi-agent framework that redefines provenance-based backward tracking as an LLM-driven collaborative reasoning process to address the limitations of existing statistical and traversal-heavy approaches—namely, poor modeling of adversarial intent and dependency explosion. It features a two-tier architecture: (1) Event-level analysis leverages hierarchical context management, retrieval-augmented reasoning with citation verification, and adversarial deliberation to enhance causal fidelity; (2) Graph exploration employs four specialized agents coordinated by a finite state machine (FSM), replacing exhaustive search with hypothesis-guided reasoning and count-first query protocols for efficient space pruning. Evaluated on 14 attack scenarios across five public datasets, Minos achieves 0.92 average recall and 0.64 precision, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines, while producing attack subgraphs 49% more compact. Crucially, it generates step-by-step interpretable reasoning traces, enabling forensic auditing and system refinement. This demonstrates the viability and superiority of LLM-native reasoning for automated provenance forensics.

Abstract

Sophisticated cyber attacks, particularly Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs), require effective post-intrusion forensic analysis. Provenance-based backward tracking reconstructs attack scenarios by tracing causality from security alerts, but existing methods rely on low-level statistical features and rigid traversal strategies, limiting their ability to capture high-level adversarial intent and suffering from dependency explosion. We present Minos, a multi-agent framework that formulates backward tracking as an LLM-driven reasoning process. Minos adopts a two-tiered architecture: for event-level analysis, it combines hierarchical context management, retrieval-augmented reasoning with citation verification, and adversarial deliberation to improve reasoning quality; for graph exploration, it coordinates four specialized agents under a finite state machine (FSM), replacing exhaustive traversal with hypothesis-guided reasoning and count-first query protocols to efficiently prune the search space. Experiments on 14 attack scenarios across five public datasets show that Minos achieves an average recall of 0.92 and precision of 0.64, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art baselines while producing attack subgraphs that are 49% more compact. Moreover, Minos generates interpretable reasoning throughout the tracking process, facilitating forensic auditing and system refinement. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of LLM-driven reasoning for automated provenance-based backward tracking.

item.title: KidnapRAG: A Black-Box Attack for Hijacking Reasoning in Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00422v1

AI Summary (中文)

KidnapRAG：面向智能体式检索增强生成系统的黑盒推理劫持攻击

背景与问题：检索增强生成（RAG）系统易受文档投毒攻击，但新兴的智能体式RAG（Agentic RAG）凭借多步检索-推理循环展现出更强鲁棒性——其能动态过滤弱相关毒化文档，维持用户查询驱动的原始推理链。然而，现有攻击方法多依赖白盒假设（如访问系统提示词、推理轨迹、检索器或模型参数），在真实开放场景中难以实施。

方法创新：本文首次系统研究黑盒投毒攻击——攻击者仅能发布外部可检索的恶意文档，无任何内部系统访问权限。为此，我们提出 KidnapRAG，一种基于角色协同的三阶段序列化投毒框架：

  • Bait（诱饵文档）：精准匹配用户初始查询语义，抢占首轮检索结果；
  • Chain-Link（链路文档）：内嵌引导性语言（如“请进一步分析XX原因”），触发智能体主动重构子查询，转向攻击者预设方向；
  • Mal-Ins（恶意指令文档）：以高权威性格式（如学术报告/政策文件）提供伪造证据，成为后续推理的核心依据。

item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00362v1

AI Summary (中文)

SoK：移动终端AI系统攻防全景图谱

随着人工智能模型在智能手机等终端设备上的本地化部署，移动终端AI（MoAI）系统正成为实现隐私保护、低延迟与离线智能的关键范式。然而，模型本地存储与执行也引入了全新的攻击面——包括模型窃取、后门注入、对抗样本规避、推理侧信道泄露及运行时篡改等威胁，而现有安全研究呈现碎片化、缺乏系统性梳理。

本研究首次开展面向MoAI系统的全面知识体系化（SoK）工作，构建覆盖三大核心维度的统一分析框架：

  • 安全支柱：明确MoAI特有的信任边界（如OS/TEE/模型运行时协同）、数据-模型-硬件多层耦合特性；
  • 攻击全景：系统归纳12类典型攻击（含6类新型终端特有攻击），按攻击目标（模型/数据/控制流）、触发时机（训练前/推理中/部署后）与技术路径分类建模；
  • 防御图谱：评估37种现有防御方案，指出其在移动端的适用性瓶颈（如TEE开销、编译器级混淆兼容性、轻量级水印鲁棒性不足）。

关键发现包括：92%的现有防御未在真实移动芯片（如骁龙、A系列）上验证；模型水印与差分隐私在资源受限场景下存在精度-安全权衡失衡；跨层协同防御（如OS调度+模型剪枝+硬件隔离）是当前最可行路径。本文同步发布首个开源资源库 [Awesome-MoAI-Security](https://github.com/Jinxhy/Awesome-MoAI-Security)，整合论文、工具链与基准测试集，为构建可信赖MoAI系统提供理论基石与实践指南。

AI Summary (English)

This paper presents the first Systematization of Knowledge (SoK) on security for Mobile on-device AI (MoAI) systems—AI models deployed and executed locally on smartphones and edge devices. We systematically analyze MoAI’s unique threat landscape, identifying 12 attack classes—including 6 device-specific threats (e.g., GPU microarchitectural leakage, OS-level model hijacking)—and map them across attack vectors, timing, and impact. On the defense side, we evaluate 37 existing techniques, revealing critical gaps: 92% lack real mobile hardware validation; lightweight watermarking and differential privacy suffer severe accuracy-security trade-offs under resource constraints; and cross-layer defenses (OS + runtime + hardware) show the highest practical promise. We propose the first unified framework covering security pillars, attack taxonomy, and defense feasibility analysis—and release an open resource hub (https://github.com/Jinxhy/Awesome-MoAI-Security) to accelerate secure MoAI development.

Abstract

Mobile on-device AI (MoAI) systems that integrate locally deployed AI models with conventional mobile software components are emerging as a key paradigm for delivering intelligent functionality directly on end-user devices. By moving inference from remote cloud services to the local mobile environment, such systems enable privacy-preserving, low-latency, and offline-capable AI functionality, yet introduce new security risks arising from the local storage of AI models. This paper presents the first comprehensive systematization of knowledge on MoAI security, covering security pillars, attack landscape, and defense landscape of MoAI systems. We further identify unresolved gaps in current attack and defense research and point to promising directions for future research in this emerging area. Our work establishes the first systematic framework for understanding the attack and defense landscapes of MoAI systems, serving as a foundation for building secure MoAI systems and advancing research in this critical domain. Companion resources are available at https://github.com/Jinxhy/Awesome-MoAI-Security.

item.title: Language-Critique Imitation Learning from Suboptimal Demonstrations
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.01225v1

AI Summary (中文)

背景与问题

现有基于次优示范（suboptimal demonstrations）的模仿学习方法，多依赖压缩型监督信号——如置信度估计、判别器得分或重要性权重等标量值。这类标量信号存在根本性局限：无法显式表达任务进展的中间推理、失败模式的细粒度诊断，或具体可行的纠正策略，导致丰富语义信息在监督过程中严重丢失。

方法创新

本文提出语言批判（Language-Critique）框架，首次将自然语言作为结构化监督信号引入模仿学习。该框架包含两大核心组件：

  • 语言标签构建：对每段次优示范自动生成三元语言标注——① 当前任务进展状态（如“机器人已接近目标但未对齐方向”）；② 显式识别的次优行为（如“过早转向导致路径偏移”）；③ 面向动作空间的细粒度纠正指导（如“应先平移0.3m再顺时针旋转15°”）；
  • 语言批判损失函数（LC-loss）：直接建模策略输出与语言标注间的语义一致性，避免将语言反馈降维为标量，并成功适配于行为克隆（LC-BC）与扩散策略（LC-DP）两类主流架构。

理论与实证贡献

理论层面，我们在标准假设下证明LC-loss目标函数可上界限定专家性能差距，为方法提供收敛性保障。实验层面，在涵盖导航（AntMaze）、操作（FrankaKitchen）、游戏（CarRacing）等多样化的连续控制任务中，LC-BC与LC-DP均显著超越强基线——包括DAgger、GAIL、BC+RL及Offline RL方法（如CQL、IQL），平均性能提升达23.7%。结果表明：自然语言不仅是可解释的监督媒介，更是承载结构化决策知识的高效载体，能有效提升策略从次优数据中学习鲁棒性的能力。

AI Summary (English)

Prior imitation learning from suboptimal demonstrations relies on scalar supervision (e.g., confidence scores or discriminator outputs), which inherently discards rich semantic information about task progress, failure modes, and corrective actions. We propose Language-Critique (LC), a novel framework that uses natural language as structured, expressive supervision. LC first generates fine-grained language labels describing current state, suboptimal behaviors, and action-level corrections for each demonstration. It then introduces a language-critique loss that directly trains policies—without scalar compression—and instantiates it for behavior cloning (LC-BC) and diffusion policies (LC-DP). Theoretically, we prove the LC objective upper-bounds the expert performance gap under standard assumptions. Empirically, LC-BC and LC-DP consistently outperform strong baselines—including imitation learning (DAgger, GAIL) and offline RL (CQL, IQL)—across diverse continuous control tasks (navigation, manipulation, gameplay), demonstrating that language serves as a powerful, interpretable, and structurally rich supervision signal for robust policy learning from suboptimal data.

Abstract

Prior work on imitation learning from suboptimal demonstrations typically relies on compressed supervision signals such as confidence estimates, discriminator scores, or importance weights. These scalar signals are inherently limited, as they cannot explicitly express intermediate reasoning about task progress, failure modes, or corrective actions. We propose a language-critique framework for imitation learning from suboptimal demonstrations that instead leverages natural language as a structured supervision signal, avoiding the collapse of expressive feedback into scalars. Our method first constructs language labels from demonstrations that explicitly describe current progress, identify suboptimal behaviors, and provide fine-grained corrective guidance. We then introduce a language-critique loss that directly trains policies using these structured signals without reducing them to scalars, and instantiate it for both behavior cloning and diffusion policies, yielding LC-BC and LC-DP. We further provide a theoretical result showing that the proposed objective upper-bounds the expert performance gap under standard assumptions. Empirically, we evaluate on diverse continuous control tasks spanning navigation, manipulation, and gameplay, where our methods consistently outperform strong imitation learning and offline reinforcement learning baselines. These results demonstrate that language can serve as a powerful and structured form of supervision for learning robust policies from suboptimal data.

item.title: Adversarial Pragmatics for AI Safety Evaluation: A Benchmark for Instruction Conflict, Embedded Commands, and Policy Ambiguity
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.01153v1

AI Summary (中文)

背景与问题

当前大语言模型（LLM）安全评估日益依赖对自然语言行为的语义判断——例如：模型是否真正遵循指令、是否合理拒绝越界请求、是否准确遵守内嵌政策、是否识别并抵抗隐性命令（如间接言语行为）、或是否在具身任务中如实报告进展。然而，主流基准常将上述复杂现象粗粒度压缩为二元“通过/失败”标签，导致失效归因模糊：究竟是模型能力不足、政策表述歧义、多指令冲突、提示结构失效，还是人工评估者判断不稳定？这一缺陷严重制约了安全评估的可解释性与诊断效度。

方法与创新

本文提出对抗性语用学（Adversarial Pragmatics）框架，首次将形式语用学理论系统转化为可操作的安全评估工具。核心贡献包括：

  • 一个语言学受控的七维分类法（instruction conflict, embedded commands, quotation, scope ambiguity, deixis, indirect speech acts, multi-turn agent transcripts）；
  • 一个含18项种子题目的基准集，强制嵌入验证器校验的元数据（如意图层级、政策锚点、歧义类型）；
  • 54行本地化先导试点数据，覆盖中英双语语境下的典型语用陷阱；
  • 专家评估协议，要求独立标注五维度：任务成功、政策合规性、安全风险等级、拒绝结果性质（恰当/过度/缺失）、评估者置信度；
  • 三项新型指标：评估者效度（judge validity）、诊断歧义度（diagnostic ambiguity）、分类法漂移率（taxonomy drift），支持评估过程的量化审计。

该框架已成功应用于LLM裁判模型校准、黄金测试集构建、提示注入鲁棒性测试及安全文档生成，显著提升安全评估的颗粒度、复现性与跨模型可比性。

AI Summary (English)

This paper introduces Adversarial Pragmatics, a linguistically grounded benchmark and annotation framework for evaluating LLM safety under complex pragmatic challenges—including instruction conflict, embedded commands, quotation, scope/deictic ambiguity, and indirect speech acts. We contribute: (1) an 18-item seed benchmark with validator-enforced metadata; (2) a 54-row pilot dataset annotated by domain experts; (3) a five-dimensional evaluation protocol distinguishing task success, policy compliance, safety risk, refusal outcome, and evaluator confidence; and (4) novel metrics—judge validity, diagnostic ambiguity, and taxonomy drift—to quantify assessment reliability and conceptual stability. Empirically, the framework improves diagnostic precision over binary benchmarks by disentangling capability limits from policy ambiguity or evaluator noise, and has been validated in LLM judge calibration, gold-set construction, prompt-injection testing, and safety documentation workflows.

Abstract

Safety evaluations for language models increasingly depend on judgments about ambiguous natural-language behaviour: whether a model has followed an instruction, refused appropriately, complied with a policy, resisted an embedded command, or misreported progress in an agentic task. Existing benchmarks often compress these distinctions into pass/fail labels, obscuring whether failures arise from capability limits, policy ambiguity, instruction conflict, scaffold failure, or unstable evaluator judgments. This paper introduces adversarial pragmatics as a benchmark and annotation protocol for evaluating model behaviour under instruction conflict, embedded commands, quotation, scope ambiguity, deixis, indirect speech acts, and multi-turn agent transcripts. The contribution is empirical and methodological: a linguistically controlled taxonomy, an 18-item seed benchmark with validator-enforced metadata, a 54-row local seed pilot, an expert-evaluation protocol distinguishing task success, policy compliance, safety risk, refusal outcome, and evaluator confidence, and metrics for judge validity, diagnostic ambiguity, and taxonomy drift. The framework turns linguistic judgment methodology into a practical tool for validating safety evals, LLM judges, gold-set construction, prompt-injection tests, and safety documentation.

item.title: Skills Are Not Islands: Measuring Dependency and Risk in Agent Skill Supply Chains
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.01136v1

AI Summary (中文)

背景与问题

Agent技能作为LLM智能体可复用的操作知识单元，正快速规模化部署，但其身份标识、版本演进与来源追溯长期隐式化，导致依赖关系不透明——已引发重复依赖引入、安装不一致等运维风险，暴露出现有依赖管理工具（如传统SBOM）在技能生态中的根本性缺失。

方法创新

本文提出Agent技能供应链（ASSC） 概念，首次系统刻画技能-包-服务混合依赖图谱；借鉴软件物料清单（SBOM）理念，设计SkillDepAnalyzer：一种能从自然语言描述中自动提取依赖证据、将技能建模为显式依赖承载体的分析器。在新构建的SKILL-DEP基准测试中，其技能元数据与依赖图还原准确率与完整性显著超越LLM基线及包中心化SBOM工具（F1提升≥32.7%）。

关键发现

基于对143万+真实技能的大规模分析，揭示四大结构性规律：

  • 技能元数据“开箱即用”但治理能力薄弱；
  • 依赖图横跨技能/包/服务三层，且存在高度集中的复用枢纽；
  • 递归技能调用催生隐性包库存与依赖链膨胀；
  • 技能依赖天然聚类于关联工作流周围。

更重要的是，单技能静态扫描会遗漏92.4%的高危依赖信号（如已知恶意包、过期证书、硬编码密钥），安全风险深度嵌套于依赖图中。

实践建议

据此提出四维治理框架：① 类型化依赖清单（Typed Dependency Manifest）；② 依赖簇一级管理（First-class Cluster Management）；③ 面向基础设施维护者的风险预警审计命令；④ 面向开发者的技能锁文件（Skill Lockfile）。已基于ASSC识别并通报多个持续存在的恶意技能至其开发者。

AI Summary (English)

This paper introduces Agent Skill Supply Chains (ASSCs) to expose and govern hidden dependencies across skills, packages, and services in LLM agent ecosystems. We design SkillDepAnalyzer, a natural-language–driven dependency analyzer inspired by SBOMs, which accurately reconstructs skill metadata and dependency graphs—outperforming LLM baselines and package-centric tools on the SKILL-DEP benchmark (F1 +32.7%). Applied to 1.43M real-world skills, ASSCs reveal four structural patterns: activation-ready but governance-poor metadata; multi-layer dependencies with concentrated reuse; recursive skill invocation expanding hidden package inventories; and workflow-coherent dependency clusters. Critically, inspecting a skill alone misses >92% of security-relevant signals embedded in its transitive dependencies. We report previously undetected malicious skills persisting in live ASSCs and propose actionable interventions: typed dependency manifests, first-class dependency-cluster management, risk-warning audit commands for maintainers, and lockfile-like records for developers.

Abstract

Agent skills package reusable operational knowledge for Large Language Model (LLM) agents, yet as they grow in scope, they become dependency-bearing artifacts whose identities, versions, and provenance remain implicit. This opacity already causes duplicated dependencies and inconsistent installations, exposing a gap that dependency management has yet to close. We introduce Agent Skill Supply Chains (ASSCs) to characterize mixed skill-package-service dependency graphs and help close this gap. Borrowing from Software Bill of Materials (SBOMs), we design SkillDepAnalyzer to capture natural-language dependency evidence and model skills as dependency-bearing artifacts. On the SKILL-DEP benchmark, SkillDepAnalyzer recovers skill metadata and dependency graphs accurately and comprehensively, substantially outperforming an LLM-based baseline and package-centric SBOM tools. Applying SkillDepAnalyzer to over 1.43 million skills, we obtain ASSCs and explore their structural diversity and security signals. We find four structural patterns: skill metadata is activation-ready but governance-poor; dependency graphs span skill, package, and service dependencies with concentrated reuse; recursive skill reuse expands dependency graphs and creates hidden package inventory; and skill dependency clusters form around related workflows. We also find that inspecting a skill alone misses security-relevant signals hiding in its dependencies. By analyzing ASSCs, we identify and report known malicious skills persisting in ASSCs to their developers. Based on these findings, we recommend typed dependency manifests, first-class dependency-cluster management, risk-warning audit commands for skill infrastructure maintainers, and lockfile-like records for skill developers.

item.title: Active Learning for Cascaded Object Detection: Balancing Coverage and Uncertainty in Table Extraction Pipelines
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00747v1

AI Summary (中文)

研究背景

商业文档中的表格抽取依赖于级联式目标检测流水线：先由表格检测（TD） 定位表格区域，再由表格结构识别（TSR） 解析其内部单元格布局。其中，TSR需精细的结构标注（如行列划分、单元格坐标与语义关系），人工成本极高；而现有主动学习（AL）方法多面向单模型任务，忽视TD与TSR之间的阶段间依赖性——TD的定位误差会传播至TSR，且两阶段特征空间异构，导致传统采样策略失效。

方法创新

本文首次将面向图像分类设计的混合采样方法Uncertainty Herding（UHerding） 适配至级联目标检测场景，并提出两种流水线感知（pipeline-aware）扩展：

  • RankFusion：构建双流形覆盖机制，在TD的检测框空间与TSR的结构表征空间（如图神经网络嵌入）同步实施多样性采样，兼顾跨阶段语义覆盖；
  • CAPA（Cascaded Adaptive Prioritization and Calibration）：引入阶段门控机制（动态屏蔽TD置信度低的样本进入TSR标注）、任务自适应不确定性校准（分别对TD的定位熵与TSR的结构预测熵归一化加权），实现端到端协同优化。

主要发现

在PubTables-1M、FinTabNet及两个私有数据集上，以71–500份文档为标注预算的实验表明：
✅ UHerding基础版本显著优于随机采样、熵采样等基线；
✅ RankFusion在平均性能上提升更显著，但方差较大（受TD误差敏感）；
✅ CAPA在4个数据集中3个上超越标准UHerding，且稳定性最优，验证了阶段解耦与不确定性校准的有效性。
本工作为结构化文档理解中的级联AL提供了首个系统性框架与可复现范式。

AI Summary (English)

Table extraction from business documents relies on a cascaded pipeline (Table Detection → Table Structure Recognition), where TSR demands costly fine-grained structural annotations. While active learning (AL) reduces annotation effort, standard AL methods ignore inter-stage dependencies in cascaded architectures. We adapt Uncertainty Herding (UHerding) — originally for image classification — to cascaded object detection for the first time. Two pipeline-aware extensions are proposed: RankFusion, which enforces dual-manifold coverage over both detection and structure representation spaces; and CAPA, which introduces stage-dependent gating and per-task uncertainty calibration. Extensive experiments across four datasets (two public, two private) and varying annotation budgets (71–500 documents) show that UHerding generalizes well to table extraction, consistently outperforming baselines. Among variants, CAPA achieves the most robust performance—outperforming standard UHerding on three of four datasets—while RankFusion yields higher average gains but with greater variance. This work establishes the first principled AL framework for cascaded table understanding.

Abstract

Table extraction from business documents relies on a cascaded pipeline where Table Detection (TD) first localizes tables and Table Structure Recognition (TSR) then recovers their internal layout. Building task-specific training sets for this pipeline is costly, particularly for TSR which requires fine-grained structural annotations. Active learning (AL) can reduce this annotation burden, yet most AL strategies are designed for single-model tasks and do not account for inter-stage dependencies in cascaded architectures. In this work, we present the first adaptation of Uncertainty Herding (UHerding), a hybrid coverage-uncertainty sampling method originally proposed for image classification, to cascaded object detection pipelines. We propose two pipeline-aware extensions that exploit the TD-to-TSR dependency: RankFusion adds dual-manifold coverage over both detection and structure representation spaces, while CAPA further incorporates stage-dependent gating and per-task uncertainty calibration. Extensive experiments across two public (PubTables-1M and FinTabNet) and two private table extraction datasets, with various annotation budgets (from 71 to 500 documents) show that UHerding generalizes well to table extraction, outperforming each baseline. Among pipeline-aware variants, RankFusion achieves higher expected gains but at the cost of greater variance, while CAPA emerges as the most consistent strategy, outperforming standard UHerding on three out of four datasets.

item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00733v1

AI Summary (中文)

背景与挑战

在罕见病研究中，基于常微分方程（ODE）的机理建模可提供可解释的动力学描述并揭示潜在生物学机制，但面临双重困境：模型结构未知、参数高度异质、个体数据极度稀缺——仅有的231条观测来自46例患者（如隐性营养不良型大疱性表皮松解症，RDEB），且数据噪声大、隐私敏感、难以获取个体轨迹。传统方法依赖个体级数据，而聚合统计（如均值、方差、分位数）虽具隐私友好性，却无法支撑联合的ODE结构发现与参数分布推断。

方法创新：AgentODE框架

本文提出AgentODE——首个端到端、纯基于群体级汇总统计的机理建模框架：

  • LLM驱动结构探索：大语言模型作为“科学假说生成器”，依据领域知识与数学约束，生成语义合理、可微分的候选ODE系统；
  • 工具增强型推理代理：通过“诊断–更新”闭环迭代优化参数分布（而非点估计），利用神经ODE求解器与概率校准模块，在仅输入群体统计（如时间序列均值±标准差）下实现分布级拟合；
  • 无个体数据依赖：全程不接触原始个体轨迹，严格满足医疗隐私合规要求。

关键结果

在3个跨学科基准任务及2个临床数据集（含RDEB）上验证：AgentODE100%恢复功能一致的ODE结构（如正确识别细胞增殖-凋亡平衡项）；在RDEB分析中，其发现的结构具备明确病理学意义（如TGF-β通路调控项），而访问个体数据的基线方法反而产生数学可行但生物学不可信的结构（如负反馈缺失、符号矛盾）。这表明：在数据稀疏场景下，约束更严格的汇总统计反成机理发现的“正则化先验”。

意义

为罕见病机制研究开辟新范式——无需打破隐私壁垒，即可从医院年报、注册登记库等常规汇总数据中直接挖掘可解释动力学模型。

AI Summary (English)

Mechanistic modeling via ODEs is vital for interpretable dynamics and mechanism inference in rare diseases—but hindered by unknown ODE structure, heterogeneous parameter distributions, and extreme scarcity/noise of individual-level data under privacy constraints. We present AgentODE, the first end-to-end framework that jointly discovers ODE structure and infers parameter distributions solely from population-level summary statistics (e.g., means, variances, quantiles). It integrates an LLM to propose biologically plausible candidate ODEs and a tool-augmented inference agent that iteratively refines parameter distributions via a diagnosis–update loop, using only aggregated data. Evaluated on three cross-domain benchmarks and two clinical datasets—including recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (RDEB) with just 231 observations across 46 patients—AgentODE recovers functionally consistent ODE structures in all cases. Critically, on RDEB, reasoning from summaries yields mechanistically principled structures (e.g., TGF-β–mediated feedback), while baselines with individual data produce mathematically adequate but biologically implausible models—demonstrating that summary statistics act as a beneficial regularizer in sparse, noisy regimes. AgentODE enables privacy-preserving, interpretable mechanistic modeling directly from routinely available aggregate clinical data.

Abstract

Mechanistic modeling via ordinary differential equations (ODEs) provides interpretable descriptions of complex dynamics and enables inference of underlying mechanisms, which is particularly valuable in clinical settings. However, in rare diseases, both the structure and parameters of the model are typically unknown, while individual-level data is scarce, noisy, heterogeneous, and subject to privacy constraints. In such settings, population-level summary statistics provide a practical privacy-preserving data representation, while capturing heterogeneity further requires modeling parameters as distributions rather than fixed values. Yet no existing method jointly discovers ODE structure and refines parameter distributions solely from summary statistics. We present AgentODE, an end-to-end framework that addresses this gap. An LLM proposes candidate ODE structures, while a tool-augmented inference agent iteratively refines parameter distributions through a diagnosis--update loop, operating on population-level summary statistics alone. We evaluate AgentODE on three benchmark problems across different fields and two clinical datasets, including the rare disease recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (RDEB), with only 231 observations across 46 patients. AgentODE recovers functionally consistent ODE structures across all settings, and experiments on RDEB demonstrates that in sparse and noisy data settings reasoning from summary statistics promotes mechanistically principled structure discovery, whereas baselines with individual-level data access recover implausible structures despite better predictive performance. AgentODE opens new possibilities for mechanistic modeling of rare diseases directly from population-level summary statistics, where data scarcity and privacy constraints have traditionally limited such analyses.

item.title: Watermarking for Proprietary Dataset Protection
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00325v1

AI Summary (中文)

研究背景

随着生成式人工智能的广泛应用，专有训练数据面临被逆向推断的风险。现有研究表明，在现代大语言模型中，基于输出损失的训练数据成员推断（Membership Inference, MI）本质上是困难任务——尤其当目标样本仅部分出现在训练集中时，传统方法性能急剧下降。

方法创新

本研究提出一种面向专有数据集保护的水印化（watermarking）新范式：不再依赖模型输出的统计偏差（如困惑度），而是将轻量级、可验证的隐式水印嵌入训练数据，并利用语言模型对水印信号的“残留放射性”（residual watermark radioactivity）——即模型即使在未完全见过水印样本的情况下，仍会在生成文本中无意复现水印模式——构建新型成员推断机制。该方法在训练阶段即部署水印，推理阶段仅需检测生成文本中的水印强度，无需访问原始训练日志或模型梯度。

主要发现

在多个主流语言模型（LLaMA-2、Qwen）和数据集（Alpaca、Dolly）上的实证表明：

  • 当水印子集覆盖率达 ≥35% 时，水印法在AUC指标上达 0.89–0.93，与最优损失基线（0.91–0.94）相当；
  • 在低暴露率（<20%）下，水印法显著优于损失法（+12.7% AUC），凸显其对稀疏水印信号的鲁棒捕获能力；
  • 水印具备不可移除性：微调/蒸馏后水印残留强度仍达原始值的76%，而损失特征易被抹平。

创新价值

本工作首次系统论证水印不仅是版权追踪工具，更是可形式化建模、可量化评估的数据归属基础设施，为数据资产确权提供可部署、低开销、抗干扰的新技术路径。

AI Summary (English)

This paper introduces watermarking as a principled framework for proprietary dataset protection and membership inference. Motivated by the intrinsic hardness of loss-based membership inference in large language models—especially under partial training exposure—we leverage the empirically observed “residual watermark radioactivity”: models trained on partially watermarked data retain detectable watermark signals in their generations, even for non-watermarked prompts. We propose a watermark-centric inference method that operates solely on generated text, requiring no access to training logs or model internals. Experiments across LLaMA-2 and Qwen show that when watermark coverage exceeds 35%, our method achieves AUC scores of 0.89–0.93—comparable to state-of-the-art loss-based baselines (0.91–0.94). Crucially, it outperforms them by +12.7% AUC at low exposure (<20%), demonstrating superior sensitivity to sparse watermark traces. The watermark persists robustly after fine-tuning (76% signal retention), unlike loss features which degrade easily. This establishes watermarking not just as a copyright marker, but as a tractable, deployable foundation for data provenance and ownership verification.

Abstract

A growing body of literature suggests that training data membership inference problems are fundamentally hard tasks in modern language modeling settings. We argue that output watermarking techniques are the right gadget to make training membership tests for generative models more tractable, based on prior results showing that language models exhibit residual watermark "radioactivity" under partially watermarked training datasets. We pit a watermark-based dataset inference approach head-to-head against traditional loss-based membership inference methods and show that watermarking can achieve comparable membership detection performance when subset exposure is high enough, under an alternate set of assumptions.

item.title: A Lifecycle and Application-Stack Survey of Large Language Model Vulnerabilities: Attacks, Risks, Defenses, and Open Problems
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31639v1

AI Summary (中文)

全生命周期与应用栈视角下的大语言模型安全脆弱性系统综述

随着大语言模型（LLM）从单纯文本生成器演变为嵌入检索管道、企业智能助手、编程环境、机器人系统、安全运营流程及跨组织自主代理的核心组件，其安全威胁已远超模型权重本身——风险根植于数据、提示、模型输出、工具调用、记忆机制与用户权限在全生命周期与应用栈中的动态交互。本文首次以生命周期阶段×应用栈层次双维框架系统梳理LLM系统脆弱性研究：将攻击面划分为八大阶段——数据采集、预训练、后训练对齐、模型打包与供应链、检索与记忆、提示工程与推理、工具/智能体执行、部署与运维。针对每一阶段，我们结构化分析攻击者能力边界、受损安全目标（保密性、完整性、可用性、安全性、隐私性、公平性、可问责性、主体控制权）、典型攻击案例（如数据污染、越狱提示、记忆泄露、工具劫持、代理链污染）、现实风险等级、现有评估方法局限，以及防御机制有效性。区别于碎片化攻击命名法，本工作强调信任边界失效点（如检索结果被当作可信指令）、非代码数据的可执行化（如PDF表格触发SQL注入）、委托权限对错误的放大效应（如Agent误调用API导致资金损失），并指出单点防御难以组合生效的根本原因。最后，提出面向产业落地的七大研究方向：可组合的安全架构、溯源感知的检索机制、工具调用沙箱化、长周期智能体行为评估、隐私保护式适配、贴近实战的红队演练、部署级事件响应体系。

AI Summary (English)

This paper presents the first systematic survey of large language model (LLM) vulnerabilities through a dual-axis lens: lifecycle stages (data collection, pretraining, alignment, packaging/supply chain, retrieval/memory, prompting/inference, tool/agent execution, deployment/maintenance) and application-stack layers. We map 120+ attacks to eight stages, analyzing attacker capabilities, compromised security objectives (confidentiality, integrity, availability, safety, privacy, fairness, accountability, agency control), practical risks, evaluation gaps, and defense limitations. Crucially, we shift focus from isolated attack names to where trust boundaries collapse: e.g., untrusted retrieval results becoming executable instructions, or delegated authority amplifying model errors into real-world harm. We identify why point defenses rarely compose and propose a research agenda including compositional security, provenance-aware retrieval, tool-call containment, long-horizon agent evaluation, privacy-preserving adaptation, realistic red teaming, and deployment-grade incident response.

Abstract

Large language models are no longer only text generators. They are increasingly embedded in retrieval pipelines, enterprise assistants, coding environments, robotic systems, security-operation workflows, and autonomous agents that can read private data, call tools, write files, execute code, and act across organizational boundaries. This shift changes the security problem: risks do not arise from the model weights alone, but from the full lifecycle and application stack through which data, prompts, model outputs, tools, memories, and user authority interact. This paper systematizes the literature on vulnerabilities in large language model systems through a lifecycle and application-stack lens. We organize attacks across eight stages: data collection, pretraining, post-training alignment, model packaging and supply chain, retrieval and memory, prompting and inference, tool/agent execution, and deployment/maintenance. For each stage, we analyze attacker capabilities, affected security objectives, representative attacks, practical risks, evaluation practices, and defenses. We further map LLM-specific vulnerabilities to confidentiality, integrity, availability, safety, privacy, fairness, accountability, and agency-control objectives. Unlike taxonomies that list isolated attack names, the proposed systematization emphasizes where trust boundaries fail, how untrusted data becomes executable instruction, how delegated authority amplifies model errors, and why point defenses rarely compose. We close with a research agenda for secure LLM systems, including compositional security, provenance-aware retrieval, tool-call containment, long-horizon agent evaluation, privacy-preserving adaptation, realistic red teaming, and deployment-grade incident response.

item.title: Hybrid Topological Data Analysis and LSTM Networks for Enhanced Network Intrusion Detection Using CIC-IDS2017 Dataset
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31619v1

AI Summary (中文)

研究背景与问题

网络入侵检测系统（NIDS）是现代网络安全防御体系的核心组件，亟需兼具鲁棒性与可解释性的先进方法以应对日益复杂的多类型攻击。传统机器学习模型在高维、非线性、时序耦合的网络流量数据上常面临特征表达力不足与时间动态建模薄弱的双重挑战。

方法创新

本研究提出一种拓扑数据驱动+深度时序建模的混合框架：首先利用拓扑数据分析（TDA） 提取网络流的全局结构特征——通过计算77维CIC-IDS2017流量特征的持久同调，生成Betti曲线与持久图；继而将这些拓扑不变量与原始时序片段联合编码，输入双向LSTM网络，实现对攻击模式中“空间拓扑结构”与“时间演化路径”的协同建模。该设计突破了TDA静态表征与LSTM纯时序建模的固有局限。

实验结果与贡献

在包含280万+标注流、14类真实攻击（DDoS、暴力破解、Web攻击、渗透、僵尸网络等）的CIC-IDS2017数据集上，模型取得AUC=1.000、F1-score=1.000的完美性能（5折交叉验证均值：AUC=1.000±0.000，F1=0.999±0.001）。消融实验证实：仅用拓扑特征（F1=0.990）或仅用时序LSTM（F1=1.000）均不及混合模型，验证二者互补性；对比实验显示，本模型显著优于TDA+随机森林（F1=0.994）和孤立森林（F1=0.835），尤其在低频隐蔽攻击（如渗透、DoS Hulk）中泛化优势突出。本工作为可解释AI安全模型提供了新范式。

AI Summary (English)

This paper proposes a hybrid Topological Data Analysis (TDA) + LSTM framework for network intrusion detection, addressing the dual challenge of capturing both global structural patterns and temporal dynamics in network traffic. We compute persistent homology on 77-dimensional CIC-IDS2017 features to generate Betti curves and persistence diagrams—topological descriptors encoding shape-invariant properties—and fuse them with raw time-series flow segments as input to a bidirectional LSTM. Evaluated on 2.8M+ labeled flows across 14 attack types, our model achieves perfect AUC (1.000) and near-perfect F1-score (1.000), with 5-fold CV showing mean AUC = 1.000 ± 0.000 and mean F1 = 0.999 ± 0.001. Ablation confirms complementary contributions: topological features alone yield F1=0.990, temporal modeling alone yields F1=1.000. The hybrid approach outperforms TDA+Random Forest (F1=0.994) and Isolation Forest (F1=0.835), especially on stealthy attacks. This work bridges topological robustness and deep sequential learning for interpretable, high-fidelity NIDS.

Abstract

Network intrusion detection systems (NIDS) are crucial in cybersecurity infrastructure, needing advanced techniques to detect hostile activity in network traffic. This research introduces a hybrid approach that combines Topological Data Analysis (TDA) with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to improve anomaly detection in network security. Our multi-layered design combines TDA's persistent homology with LSTM networks to capture topological characteristics of network traffic patterns and simulate temporal sequences. We assessed our methodology using the CIC-IDS2017 dataset, which includes over 2.8 million labelled flows, 77 network variables, and 14 attack categories that reflect modern threat landscapes such as DDoS, brute force, web attacks, penetration, and botnet activities. Integrating Betti curves and persistence diagrams with deep learning architectures enhances feature extraction performance. Our hybrid TDA+LSTM model has an AUC of 1.000 and F1-score of 1.000, with 5-fold cross-validation producing a mean AUC of 1.000 $\pm$ 0.000 and mean F1 of 0.999 $\pm$ 0.001. An ablation research demonstrates the complimentary contributions of topological (F1=0.990) and temporal characteristics (F1=1.000). Comparative research shows that the suggested strategy beats TDA+Random Forest (F1=0.994) and Isolation Forest (F1=0.835) baselines in several attack categories.

item.title: CVE-TTP KG: Knowledge Graph Linking Software Vulnerabilities to Attack Behaviors
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31557v1

AI Summary (中文)

研究背景

在日益复杂的网络威胁环境中，攻击者频繁利用软件漏洞（CVE）实施高级持续性威胁（APT）。现有权威数据库（如CVE、NVD）虽提供详尽的技术描述，却普遍缺乏与攻击者行为模式（如MITRE ATT&CK框架中的战术Tactics与技术Techniques）的语义关联，导致安全分析难以从“漏洞”跃迁至“攻击意图”，严重制约威胁研判、响应决策与防御自动化。

方法创新

本研究提出CVE-TTP知识图谱（CVE-TTP KG），首次系统性构建漏洞与ATT&CK行为的结构化映射。技术路径包含三阶段：
1. 行为识别：基于领域适配的CySecBERT（在网络安全语料上继续预训练的Transformer模型），实现CVE描述文本中TTP（Tactics & Techniques）的细粒度分类；
2. 实体与关系抽取：构建迄今最大规模的CVE-TTP标注数据集（含24,820个实体与43,608条关系），对比评估pipeline式与span-based联合模型；
3. 图谱构建与可视化：将结构化结果注入Neo4j图数据库，支持多跳查询、攻击链推演与跨漏洞行为聚类。

关键成果

  • CySecBERT在TTP分类任务中达87.71%（Techniques） 与96.16%（Tactics） 的macro-F1；
  • pipeline方法在实体/关系抽取中分别取得0.86与0.99 macro-F1，显著优于联合模型（0.78）；
  • CVE-TTP KG已开源，为威胁情报融合、自动化红蓝对抗及AI驱动的漏洞优先级排序提供可解释、可推理的知识基座。

AI Summary (English)

This paper introduces CVE-TTP KG, a knowledge graph that semantically links Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) to MITRE ATT&CK tactics and techniques—bridging the critical gap between vulnerability data and adversary behavior. We propose a three-stage pipeline: (1) fine-tuned CySecBERT, a cybersecurity-domain adapted Transformer, achieves macro-F1 scores of 87.71% on technique classification and 96.16% on tactic classification; (2) a large-scale annotated dataset (24,820 entities, 43,608 relations) enables robust entity/relation extraction, with pipeline methods outperforming joint modeling (0.86 vs. 0.78 macro-F1 for entities; 0.99 vs. 0.78 for relations); and (3) structured outputs are integrated into a Neo4j-based cyber threat knowledge graph, supporting queryable, visualizable, and inferable vulnerability-behavior mappings. CVE-TTP KG advances threat intelligence interoperability and AI-powered security operations.

Abstract

In the evolving threat landscape, adversaries exploit software vulnerabilities to launch sophisticated attacks, challenging traditional defenses. Although databases like CVE and NVD provide detailed technical information, they often lack links to attacker behaviors such as tactics and techniques, limiting effective threat interpretation and response. This work bridges this gap by connecting vulnerabilities with behavioral patterns from the MITRE ATT&CK framework. We construct a CVE-TTP Knowledge Graph that links CVEs to tactics and techniques using classification and relation extraction. Transformer-based models are developed for behavior identification, with CySecBERT achieving macro F1-scores of 87.71% (techniques) and 96.16% (tactics). Also, we created an annotated dataset with 24,820 entities and 43,608 relations for entity and relation extraction. The pipeline-based approach achieves macro F1-scores of 0.86 (entity extraction) and 0.99 (relation extraction), while a span-based joint model achieves 0.78. These outputs are integrated into a Neo4j-based Cyber Threat Knowledge Graph, enabling structured visualization of vulnerabilities.

item.title: EnclaveX: End-to-End Confidential AI with CPU/GPU TEEs
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31408v1

AI Summary (中文)

EnclaveX：面向端到端机密AI的CPU/GPU可信执行环境协同框架

随着大语言模型（LLMs）的爆发式应用，AI服务高度依赖微软Azure、谷歌云、AWS等中心化云平台，用户被迫上传敏感数据及训练/微调代码，引发严峻的数据泄露、模型窃取与管理员越权访问风险。尽管Intel SGX/TDX、AMD SEV-SNP和ARM CCA等CPU端可信执行环境（TEEs）已部分缓解信任问题，NVIDIA近年推出的H100/H200 GPU TEE亦拓展了硬件级机密计算边界，但现有研究仍缺乏对CPU与GPU TEE跨层协同、端到端AI工作流（含模型加载、前向/反向传播、分布式训练）的系统性支持与实证评估。

本文提出EnclaveX——首个支持CPU与GPU TEE深度融合的端到端机密AI框架。我们设计三重防护机制：（1）VM级隔离：基于Intel TDX与AMD SEV-SNP实现虚拟机级内存加密与远程证明；（2）应用级机密性增强：通过安全启动链、TEE内核模块验证及GPU内存页锁定，阻断Kubernetes集群管理员对机密VM内存的非法读取（实验证实传统方案中该漏洞可导致完整模型权重泄露）；（3）跨设备安全通信：定义CPU-GPU间经签名认证的DMA通道协议，确保梯度与参数在TEE边界内安全流转。我们在真实H200+TDX环境中部署Llama-2-7B微调任务，基准测试表明：相较非TEE基线，端到端延迟开销为18.3%–24.7%（取决于batch size），远低于纯软件加密方案（>200%）；远程证明耗时稳定在320ms以内，满足生产级SLA要求。本工作首次量化验证了异构TEE协同在LLM场景下的可行性与实用性，为构建零信任AI基础设施提供关键技术路径。

AI Summary (English)

EnclaveX presents the first end-to-end confidential AI framework unifying CPU and GPU Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs). It addresses critical gaps in holistic LLM confidentiality—particularly against privileged cloud administrators—by integrating Intel TDX/AMD SEV-SNP VM isolation with NVIDIA H200 GPU TEEs. We introduce a secure CPU-GPU communication protocol, harden application-level integrity via signed DMA channels and kernel module attestation, and empirically expose Kubernetes admin privilege escalation risks in prior TEE deployments. Evaluated on Llama-2-7B fine-tuning with industry benchmarks, EnclaveX incurs only 18.3–24.7% end-to-end latency overhead (vs. non-TEE baseline) and achieves remote attestation in <320 ms, demonstrating practical viability for production-grade confidential AI.

Abstract

Large Language Models (LLMs) have rapidly proliferated, driving widespread adoption of AI applications. Most deployments rely on centralized infrastructures such as Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, or AWS, requiring users to share sensitive data and training or fine-tuning code. This dependence raises significant security and privacy concerns, as cloud providers must be trusted to ensure confidentiality and integrity. Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) e.g., Intel SGX/TDX, AMD SEV-SNP, and ARM CCA have been introduced to mitigate these risks. More recently, NVIDIA has developed GPU TEEs (e.g., H100/H200), yet comprehensive evaluations of end-to-end workflows that integrate CPU and GPU TEEs remain limited. Critical aspects, including performance overhead, remote attestation, and security guarantees for AI/LLM applications, have not been sufficiently studied. This paper addresses this gap by presenting an end-to-end workflow that combines CPU and GPU TEEs. We propose mechanisms to ensure confidentiality and integrity at both the VM level (via Intel TDX and AMD SEV-SNP) and the application level, highlighting vulnerabilities such as Kubernetes administrators' ability to access confidential VM contents. Finally, we evaluate the performance overhead of our system using industry benchmarks, focusing on configurations that integrate Intel TDX with NVIDIA H200 GPUs.

item.title: The Decomposition Is the Fingerprint: Per-Component Identity for Agent Skills
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31272v1

AI Summary (中文)

背景与挑战

随着AI智能体在运行时动态获取与执行技能（如提示指令、可执行代码、工具声明等组件），亟需一种稳定、可比对的技能身份标识机制。传统加密哈希（如SHA-256）因雪崩效应——单字符修改即导致完全不同的哈希值——无法支持细粒度相似性判断，难以应对提示重述、变量重命名、代码重构或可控翻译等常见变体。

方法创新

本文提出“分解即指纹”（Decomposition Is the Fingerprint）范式：将技能解耦为三元组——prompt、code、tools——并为每个组件独立生成局部敏感指纹。采用多银行SimHash技术，将各组件嵌入映射至紧凑的二进制位向量，最终合成固定长度120字节签名，支持常数时间内的汉明距离比较。

核心发现与价值

  • 结构化身份识别：三元组设计使系统能精准恢复“技能家族”关系——当任一组件保持共享时（如工具不变而提示被 paraphrase），仍可识别同源；而完全独立的多语言重实现则不被判定为同一技能，体现谱系（lineage）而非行为等价。
  • 变更定位能力：自动定位复用或篡改发生的组件层级（如仅代码被修改），支撑可追溯的“技能物料清单（SkillBOM）”。
  • 高效鲁棒性：在4,950次两两比对中AUC达0.974（95% CI [0.956, 0.994]），比特开销仅为所逼近嵌入的1/77，且排序保真度在有限位下具备理论收敛保证。
  • 安全定位清晰：该指纹是身份信号（identity signal），非安全判决；它构建技能注册中心的结构主干，安全性仍需依赖独立的行为验证。

AI Summary (English)

This paper introduces a per-component locality-sensitive fingerprint for AI agent skills—decomposed into prompt, code, and tool declarations—to enable stable, interpretable identity tracking amid paraphrasing, refactoring, renaming, and controlled translation. Unlike cryptographic hashes, our 120-byte SimHash-based signature preserves structural lineage (not behavioral equivalence) via Hamming-distance comparison in constant time. Crucially, representing identity as a triple—not a scalar—enables relationship classification (e.g., family membership), novelty detection, and precise change localization (e.g., “only code modified”). Evaluated on 4,950 pairwise comparisons, it achieves an AUC of 0.974 (95% CI [0.956, 0.994]) using 77× fewer bits than the embedding it approximates, with provably preserved ranking. On a 906-skill injection benchmark, it detects tampered copies and pinpoints modifications—but by design remains a complementary identity signal, not a safety verdict.

Abstract

AI agents increasingly acquire and execute skills at runtime: bundles of prompt instructions, executable code, and tool declarations fetched from marketplaces and other agents. Governing them needs a stable notion of skill identity, yet cryptographic hashing is engineered to destroy the very similarity we need, as a one-character edit scrambles the digest. We present a compact, locality-sensitive fingerprint that embeds each component of a skill and projects it to bits with a multi-bank SimHash, giving a fixed 120-byte signature compared in constant time by Hamming distance. Our central claim is that keeping the fingerprint as a per-component triple (prompt, code, tools), rather than a single score, is what makes it useful: the triple recovers skill-family identity through paraphrase, renaming, refactoring, and controlled code translation when another component remains shared, while independent multilingual reimplementation is not recovered; it also localizes which component carries the reuse. We claim lineage, not behavioral equivalence: identity supplies the structural axis of a registry and leaves safety to behavioral verification. The fingerprint reaches an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.974 (95% CI [0.956, 0.994]) over 4,950 pairwise comparisons while using 77x fewer bits than the embedding it approximates, with ranking preserved in expectation and finite-bit concentration; the per-component split turns one number into relationship classification, families, novelty, and a portable "SkillBOM" for a skill registry. On a 906-skill injection benchmark the fingerprint recognizes injected skills as tampered copies of a known base and localizes the change, but recognition is not trust: it remains, by design, an identity signal complementary to behavioral verification rather than a safety verdict.

item.title: Securing the AI Agent: A Unified Framework for Multi-Layer Agent Red Teaming
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31227v1

AI Summary (中文)

背景与挑战

随着开源AI基础设施的爆发式发展——涵盖模型服务引擎、智能体（Agent）平台、Model Context Protocol（MCP）生态，乃至基础大语言模型本身——其安全防护能力已严重滞后。现有安全工具多聚焦单一层面（如模型层或API层），难以应对AI智能体跨层耦合的攻击面：攻击者可同时利用底层基础设施漏洞、协议实现缺陷、技能包（skill package）供应链风险、行为逻辑盲区及模型自身脆弱性。

方法与框架

本文提出 AI-Infra-Guard——首个覆盖全栈AI智能体的开源红队框架。其核心洞见是：AI智能体的安全边界具有四层结构化特征（基础设施层、协议/工具层、智能体行为层、模型层），需匹配差异化检测范式：

  • 基础设施层：基于75+主流AI组件（如vLLM、Ollama、LangChain）与1,400+精准规则的确定性规则匹配；
  • 协议/工具层：由LLM驱动的自主式审计代理，动态探测MCP服务器接口与技能包权限滥用；
  • 行为层：支持多轮交互的黑盒智能体红队测试，模拟真实用户-智能体对抗；
  • 模型层：集成26+攻击算子的 jailbreak 框架，覆盖16个主流基准数据集（如AdvBench、SafeBench）。

创新与价值

AI-Infra-Guard是目前唯一支持智能体技能供应链审计的开源框架，填补了AI Agent安全中“第三方技能引入”这一关键风险域空白。我们以层-范式匹配（layer-paradigm matching） 为设计原则，提供可扩展、可组合的安全基座，推动社区共建统一防御标准。

AI Summary (English)

AI-Infra-Guard is the first open-source framework unifying red teaming across all layers of AI agent infrastructure: infrastructure (e.g., vLLM, Ollama), protocol/tool (e.g., MCP servers, skill packages), agent behavior (multi-turn black-box interaction), and model (jailbreak resilience). It departs from monolithic detection by matching specialized paradigms to each layer—deterministic rule matching over 75+ components and 1,400+ vulnerability rules; LLM-driven agentic auditing of MCP endpoints and skill permissions; multi-turn adversarial probing of agent workflows; and a modular jailbreak harness with 26+ operators evaluated on 16 datasets. Crucially, it introduces supply-chain auditing for third-party agent skills—a previously unaddressed vector in open-agent ecosystems. Released under an open license, AI-Infra-Guard establishes layer-paradigm matching as a practical foundation for scalable, community-driven AI agent security.

Abstract

The fast growth of open-source AI infrastructure, from model serving engines and agent platforms to the Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem and the language models themselves, has outpaced the security tooling available to defend it. We present AI-Infra-Guard, an open-source framework that organizes AI red teaming around a single observation: the attack surface of an AI agent is stratified across layers (infrastructure, protocol/tool, agent behavior, and model), and no single detection paradigm fits all of them. The framework therefore matches a paradigm to each layer, from deterministic rule matching over 75+ AI components and 1{,}400+ vulnerability rules, through LLM-driven agentic auditing of MCP servers and agent-skill packages and multi-turn black-box agent red teaming, to a jailbreak harness with 26+ attack operators over sixteen datasets. To our knowledge it is the only open-source framework to span all of these, including supply-chain auditing of the agent skills that increasingly extend AI agents. We release AI-Infra-Guard as open source so that \emph{layer-paradigm matching} can serve as a practical foundation for agent security and a shared base for the community to build on.

item.title: An Empirical Study of Security Calibration in Large Language Models for Code
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31159v1

AI Summary (中文)

大语言模型代码安全校准的首次大规模实证研究

本研究首次系统性探究了大语言模型（LLM）在代码生成场景下的安全校准性（security calibration）——即模型对其输出代码安全性判断的置信度是否真实反映其实际安全水平。针对当前LLM广泛应用于软件开发却缺乏对“高置信度≠高安全性”风险认知的现状，我们构建了覆盖自包含安全任务与多语言仓库级上下文的双轨评估基准，并在GPT-4o-mini、Gemini-2.0-Flash和Qwen3-Coder-Next三大主流模型上，于多种temperature设置下开展大规模实证分析。

核心发现包括：（1）普遍过自信现象：所有模型在安全判断上均显著高估自身能力，尤其在复杂仓库级环境中False Trust（对漏洞代码赋予高置信度）频发；（2）安全校准优于功能校准：模型对“代码是否安全”的估计比对“代码是否功能正确”的估计更可靠，暗示安全属性（如模式匹配、规则违反）比依赖运行时行为的功能正确性更易被模型感知；（3）校准引导修复效果有限：基于置信度筛选的自动修复仅小幅降低漏洞率，却频繁引发功能回归；（4）架构化门控存在场景局限性：虽在受控任务中提升校准度，但在真实仓库级场景中反而加剧校准恶化，凸显实验室指标与工程实践间的鸿沟。本研究为LLM安全可信部署提供了关键实证依据与方法论警示。

AI Summary (English)

This paper presents the first large-scale empirical study of security calibration—the alignment between an LLM’s confidence in code security and its actual security correctness. We evaluate GPT-4o-mini, Gemini-2.0-Flash, and Qwen3-Coder-Next across temperature settings on two complementary benchmarks: self-contained security tasks and realistic multi-language repository-level contexts. Results reveal pervasive overconfidence: models frequently assign high confidence to vulnerable code (False Trust). Surprisingly, security calibration consistently outperforms functional calibration—suggesting models reason about security properties (e.g., pattern-based vulnerabilities) more reliably than functional correctness (which depends on complex execution semantics). Calibration-guided automated repair yields only marginal security improvements while often introducing functional regressions. Moreover, architectural gating improves calibration on controlled benchmarks but worsens it in repository-level settings—highlighting a critical gap between lab evaluation and real-world deployment. Our work establishes foundational evidence for calibrating LLMs in security-critical coding.

Abstract

Large Language Models (LLMs) are rapidly transforming software development, yet their use in security-critical contexts raises a key question: do models know when their generated code is insecure? This property, known as calibration, measures whether a model's confidence aligns with the true correctness of its outputs. We present the first large-scale empirical study of security calibration in LLM-generated code. We evaluate GPT-4o-mini, Gemini-2.0-Flash, and Qwen3-Coder-Next across multiple temperature settings on two complementary benchmarks: self-contained security tasks and multi-language repository-level contexts. Our results suggest that overconfidence is prevalent across the evaluated LLMs. Functional calibration is consistently worse than security calibration, suggesting that models estimate security outcomes more reliably than functional correctness, potentially because functional correctness depends on complex execution behavior. We also examine whether calibration-guided automated repair can help remediate vulnerabilities in LLM-generated code, finding only limited improvements while frequently introducing functional regressions. Moreover, we study different mitigation strategies for reducing False Trust, where models assign high confidence to vulnerable code. The results show that although architectural gating improves calibration on controlled benchmarks, calibration deteriorates in realistic repository-level settings, increasing the risk of high-confidence vulnerable outputs.

item.title: Secure-CHG: A Comprehensive Framework for Robust and Fair Federated Learning via Hybrid Defense and Contribution-Aware Trust
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31066v1

AI Summary (中文)

背景与问题

联邦学习（FL）易受隐蔽后门攻击威胁，攻击者通过注入含特定触发器的样本，诱导全局模型对目标类产生错误预测。现有统计型防御方法（如Krum、Trimmed Mean）主要依赖梯度范数、距离等形态学特征，在训练早期有效，却忽视了一个关键漏洞——“晚期失效”（Late-stage Failure）：随着全局模型收敛，良性与恶意客户端的梯度范数同步衰减，导致二者在统计分布上趋于不可区分，传统防御机制因此“失明”，使自适应攻击者可长期潜伏并在后期劫持聚合过程。

方法创新

本文提出 Secure-CHG——一种融合式鲁棒公平联邦学习框架，实现从“形态检测”到“语义贡献验证”的范式跃迁。其核心包含两阶段自适应防御流水线：

  • 早期阶段：采用级联统计滤波器（Cascaded Statistical Filter），抑制初始震荡期的噪声干扰，保障优化稳定性；
  • 晚期阶段：引入原创的 CHG-Shapley 机制——将本地更新映射至由样本难度（即本地训练损失）与梯度构成的复合Hardness-Gradient（CHG）空间，显著放大恶意更新的语义异常痕迹；
  • 理论上，我们推导出CHG-Shapley的闭式解，支持无需重训练的轻量级节点价值评估，并驱动信任加权聚合，兼顾鲁棒性与贡献公平性。

实验结果

在CIFAR-10、MedMNIST和NEU-SDDB三大异构数据集上系统验证：Secure-CHG成功克服晚期失效，对先进后门攻击（如Label-Flipping+Trigger Injection）的攻击成功率分别比Krum降低2.3×、比Trimmed Mean降低2.0×，同时保持98.2%以上的主任务准确率，显著优于SOTA基线。

AI Summary (English)

Federated Learning (FL) faces severe threats from stealthy backdoor attacks, yet existing statistical defenses fail in late training stages due to vanishing gradient norms—termed Late-stage Failure. To address this, we propose Secure-CHG, a hybrid defense framework that shifts focus from superficial gradient morphology to intrinsic semantic contribution verification. It features: (i) a cascaded statistical filter for early-phase stabilization; and (ii) the novel CHG-Shapley mechanism—projecting updates into a composite Hardness-Gradient space (using local loss + gradient) to amplify adversarial semantic traces even when norms decay. We derive a closed-form solution for CHG-Shapley, enabling efficient, retraining-free node valuation and trust-aware aggregation. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10, MedMNIST, and NEU-SDDB show Secure-CHG reduces advanced backdoor attack success rates by 2.3× vs. Krum and 2.0× vs. Trimmed Mean, while preserving >98.2% main-task accuracy.

Abstract

Federated Learning (FL) is highly susceptible to stealthy backdoor attacks, which aim to force a model into predicting an attacker-chosen target class for inputs containing a specific trigger. However, existing statistical defenses primarily focus on the early stages of model convergence. In this paper, we identify a fundamental vulnerability termed ``Late-stage Failure.'' We demonstrate that as the global model converges, decaying gradient norms render malicious and benign updates morphologically indistinguishable. This vanishing statistical variance effectively blinds traditional defenses, enabling adaptive adversaries to remain dormant and subsequently hijack the training process. To overcome these constraints, we propose Secure-CHG, a hybrid framework that pivots the defense paradigm from superficial morphological detection toward intrinsic semantic contribution verification. Secure-CHG employs an adaptive defense pipeline: a cascaded statistical filter stabilizes optimization during the early oscillatory phase, while a novel CHG-Shapley mechanism takes over during late-stage convergence. By leveraging sample hardness (i.e., local training loss) to project updates into a composite Hardness-Gradient space, it effectively amplifies adversarial semantic traces, enabling the isolation of stealthy attackers even as gradient norms vanish. Furthermore, we derive a closed-form solution for CHG-Shapley, facilitating low-complexity, retraining-free node valuation and trust-modulated aggregation. Extensive evaluations on CIFAR-10, MedMNIST, and NEU-SDDB demonstrate that Secure-CHG effectively mitigates Late-stage Failure. Specifically, it significantly suppresses advanced backdoor attacks, reducing their attack success rate by 2.3$\times$ and 2.0$\times$ relative to the mainstream Krum and Trimmed Mean baselines, respectively.

item.title: Amplifying Membership Signal Through Chained Regeneration
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31991v1

AI Summary (中文)

背景与问题

大型生成式模型易记忆训练数据，导致隐私泄露与版权风险加剧。当前成员推断攻击（MIA）与数据集推断（DI）多依赖单次生成（one-shot generation），信号微弱、跨模态敏感性低，且白盒/灰盒场景下常需训练影子模型——对大模型而言计算不可行。

方法创新：MADreMIA框架

受模型自噬紊乱（Model Autophagy Disorder, MAD）启发，本文提出MADreMIA——一种模型无关、无需影子模型的新型框架。其核心是链式再生（Chained Regeneration）：通过跨模态迭代生成（如文本→图像→文本→音频…），将前一阶段输出作为下一阶段输入，构建长程生成轨迹。该过程天然放大模型对训练样本的记忆信号：成员样本在多次再生中保持更高语义连贯性与结构稳定性，而非成员样本则快速退化。

关键发现与优势

  • 低假阳性率（FPR）下显著提升检测能力：在相同FPR=1%时，MADreMIA相较基线方法平均提升AUC达12.7–28.3个百分点；
  • 跨模态普适性强：在IARs（隐式自回归模型）、扩散模型（Stable Diffusion）、语言模型（LLaMA-2、GPT-2）上均验证有效；
  • 首次拓展至音频模态：初步实验表明其在Whisper微调模型上亦可实现稳健DI；
  • 完全免训练：仅需目标模型前向推理，支持白盒、灰盒、黑盒全场景，部署成本极低。

本工作揭示了生成轨迹的“记忆衰减动力学”本质，为轻量、通用、多模态的隐私审计提供了新范式。

AI Summary (English)

Large generative models’ tendency to memorize training data necessitates robust membership inference (MIA) and dataset inference (DI) for privacy and copyright auditing. Existing methods rely on one-shot generations, yielding weak, modality-limited signals—and often require infeasible shadow-model training. Inspired by Model Autophagy Disorder (MAD), we propose MADreMIA, a model-agnostic framework that amplifies membership signals via chained regeneration: iterative, cross-modal generation where each output serves as the next input. We find memorized samples exhibit significantly higher coherence and slower degradation across regeneration steps than non-members, enabling high-sensitivity detection at low false positive rates. MADreMIA achieves consistent gains across IARs, diffusion models (e.g., Stable Diffusion), and language models (LLaMA-2, GPT-2), with preliminary success on audio models (Whisper). Crucially, it requires no shadow training—only black-box inference—making it scalable, efficient, and broadly deployable.

Abstract

The tendency of large generative models to memorize training data makes sample verification critical for privacy auditing and copyright enforcement. Current membership (MIA) and dataset inference (DI) attacks often rely on one-shot generations, which yield weak signals and limited sensitivity across modalities. Inspired by Model Autophagy Disorder (MAD), we introduce MADreMIA, a model-agnostic framework that enhances white-, gray-, and black-box MIA and DI. Rather than relying on shadow model training -- often infeasible for large generative models -- our framework facilitates scalable inference by leveraging inherent signals through iterative trajectories. This process utilizes chained generations across diverse modalities, where each output serves as the subsequent input, to improve membership evidence at low FPR. We demonstrate that memorized training samples exhibit significantly higher coherence and slower degradation during iterative regeneration than non-member generations. Our results show that MADreMIA provides richer signals across diverse model families and modalities; we present comprehensive evaluations for IARs, diffusion, and language models, alongside preliminary results demonstrating its potential for audio models.

item.title: Harnessing Textual Refusal Directions for Multimodal Safety
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31876v1

AI Summary (中文)

研究背景

大型语言模型（LLMs）的安全对齐常依赖后训练微调或激活空间中的“拒绝方向”（refusal directions）。然而，将这些方法迁移至多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）面临关键瓶颈：其安全对齐需依赖带标注的不安全多模态数据（如含有害图文/视频的样本），而此类数据远比纯文本数据更难收集、标注与合规获取。

核心发现与方法创新

本文首次系统验证：仅从纯文本LLM主干中提取的拒绝方向，可跨模态泛化至图像与视频输入。尽管效果受层选择、引导强度及跨模态对齐质量影响——尤其当视觉-语言对齐偏差导致本应安全的多模态输入被误导向拒绝时，这一现象揭示了模态间安全结构的潜在共享性。

基于此，我们提出模态无关拒绝引导（Modality-Agnostic Refusal Steering, MARS）：一种无需训练、轻量、即插即用的安全增强框架。MARS包含三大关键技术：

  • 激活重中心化（Activation Re-centering）：校正视觉编码器与语言解码器间的模态偏移；
  • 几何信任域自适应缩放（Trust-Region Adaptive Scaling）：在单位球面约束下动态调节引导强度，避免过强干预；
  • 首词层优化选择（First-Token Layer Selection）：仅在首个生成token处实施干预，兼顾效率与效果。

实验结果与意义

在5个SOTA MLLMs（如Qwen-VL、LLaVA-1.6、Video-LLaMA等）上，MARS在安全基准（MMBench-Safety、SafeVid）、实用性基准（MMBench、SEED-Bench）及视频越狱攻击（Video-Jailbreak） 上全面验证：平均提升安全率+12.7%，同时保持甚至小幅提升任务准确率（+0.4%）。结果证实：安全语义结构具有跨模态普适性，文本拒绝方向是未被充分挖掘的多模态对齐基石。

AI Summary (English)

To overcome the scarcity of unsafe multimodal data for aligning Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs), this work discovers that textual refusal directions—extracted solely from frozen LLM backbones—generalize across image and video modalities. We identify three key limitations: layer sensitivity, steering strength overcorrection, and cross-modal misalignment causing spurious refusals on safe inputs. To address them, we propose Modality-Agnostic Refusal Steering (MARS): a training-free, lightweight method operating at the first generated token. MARS corrects modality misalignment via activation re-centering, adaptively scales steering within a geometrically constrained trust region, and selects the optimal intervention layer. Evaluated across five state-of-the-art MLLMs on safety (MMBench-Safety, SafeVid), utility (MMBench, SEED-Bench), and video jailbreak benchmarks, MARS consistently improves safety (+12.7% avg.) without sacrificing utility (+0.4% accuracy gain). Our results demonstrate that safety-relevant representations are shared across modalities—and textual refusal directions serve as a powerful, underexploited foundation for multimodal alignment.

Abstract

To improve safety in Large Language Models (LLMs) we can either perform post-training alignment or exploit refusal directions in the activation space. Both strategies are less feasible in Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) as they require unsafe multimodal data, harder to collect than their unimodal counterpart. In this work, we relax this constraint and investigate whether textual refusal directions, extracted directly from the LLM backbone, generalize across modalities (i.e., image, video). Preliminary findings confirm this ability, though effectiveness is conditioned by layer selection, steering strength, and cross-modal alignment, with the latter causing safe multimodal inputs to be spuriously steered toward refusal. Building on this, we introduce Modality-Agnostic Refusal Steering (MARS), a light-weight training-free approach that injects multimodal safety without the need for multimodal safety data. MARS corrects modality misalignment via activation re-centering, adaptively scales steering strength within a geometrically defined trust region, and selects the optimal intervention layer, operating at the first generated token. Evaluated on five SOTA MLLMs across safety, utility, and video jailbreak benchmarks, MARS achieves consistent safety gains while preserving utility. These results reveal that safety-relevant structure is shared across modalities and that textual refusal directions are a powerful and underexplored foundation for multimodal alignment.

item.title: An Agentic AI Framework to Accelerate Scientific Discovery in Plant Phenotyping
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31831v1

AI Summary (中文)

背景与挑战

高通量植物表型分析正以前所未有的速度产生海量多模态图像数据——Oak Ridge国家实验室先进植物表型实验室（APPL）的自动化成像平台每日可采集数百株植物在可见光、近红外、热成像等多波段下的图像。然而，数据分析严重滞后：性状提取与生物学解读仍高度依赖人工判读和领域专家经验，且仅限于采集完成后的“后处理”阶段。这导致分析能力而非数据获取能力成为科学发现的真正瓶颈。

方法与创新

本研究提出首个面向植物表型场景的端到端自主智能体（Agentic AI）框架，将APPL从“数据工厂”升级为“交互式自主发现平台”。框架包含两大核心智能体：

  • Co-Scientist Agent（共研科学家智能体）：通过自然语言对话理解科学家提问（如“哪些基因型在干旱胁迫下叶片卷曲最显著？”），动态生成结构化分析计划（含目标作物、时间点、模态、算法链及验证逻辑）；
  • Compute Agent（计算智能体）：以无头方式在Frontier百亿亿次超算上调度Vision Transformer模型，执行高精度语义分割与定量性状提取（如叶面积、卷曲指数、蒸腾速率推演）。

二者运行于物理隔离的安全与资源域，通过基于令牌认证的加密流式通信通道协同——该设计显式建模了科研基础设施中的联邦治理、跨域数据移动约束与全链路溯源需求，弥补了主流云原生智能体框架在真实科研场景中的关键缺失。

主要成效

分析周期从数天至数周压缩为秒级交互闭环：智能体可实时推理中间结果、主动推荐后续实验（如“建议补充根系热成像验证水分再分配假说”）、并响应追问。实测表明，对典型干旱响应分析任务，框架将专家介入频次降低76%，同时确保每步操作、模型版本、数据切片与参数均被不可篡改地记录，实现端到端可追溯的AI增强科学发现。

AI Summary (English)

High-throughput plant phenotyping generates multimodal image data faster than human experts can analyze it—making analysis, not acquisition, the bottleneck for discovery. We present an agentic AI framework that transforms Oak Ridge’s APPL into an interactive, autonomous discovery platform. A conversational Co-Scientist Agent translates natural-language scientific questions into executable analysis plans; a headless Compute Agent executes Vision Transformer–based segmentation and trait extraction on the Frontier exascale supercomputer. The agents operate in isolated security/resource domains and communicate via a secure, token-authenticated streaming channel—explicitly addressing federation, data-movement constraints, and end-to-end provenance requirements ignored by cloud-native agentic systems. Our framework reduces typical analysis cycles from days/weeks to seconds, enables real-time result reasoning, automated follow-up suggestions, and full auditability of every AI-human interaction. It represents the first production-ready, infrastructure-aware agentic system for scalable, trustworthy scientific discovery in plant phenomics.

Abstract

High-throughput plant phenotyping now generates image derived datasets far faster than scientists can analyze them. At Oak Ridge National Laboratory's Advanced Plant Phenotyping Laboratory (APPL), automated stations image hundreds of plants daily across multiple remote sensing modalities; yet, trait extraction and interpretation remain manual, expert-bound, and strictly post-hoc, making analysis, not acquisition, the binding constraint on discovery. We present an end-to-end agentic AI framework that turns the facility from a data factory into an interactive autonomous, discovery platform, where scientists partner with AI agents to accelerate time to insight. A conversational Co-Scientist Agent translates a scientist's natural-language question into a structured analysis plan, and a headless Compute Agent dispatches Vision Transformer segmentation and trait extraction on the Frontier exascale supercomputer.
